anatomy.flutter: AlertDialog(trigger, content) -> AlertDialogContent(header, footer, size) -> AlertDialogHeader(title, description) + AlertDialogFooter(cancel, action). No AlertDialogMedia widget exists in the file at all; AlertDialogSize.sm only narrows maxWidth to Containers.xs — AlertDialogFooter's build() is a single unconditional Row(mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.end) with no branch on `size`.
anatomy.web: Exports include AlertDialogMedia (`mb-2 inline-flex size-10 ... sm:group-data-[size=default]/alert-dialog-content:row-span-2`), and AlertDialogFooter has `group-data-[size=sm]/alert-dialog-content:grid group-data-[size=sm]/alert-dialog-content:grid-cols-2` turning the footer into a 2-column grid when size="sm".

This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: Self-documented in the Flutter file's own library doc: "Not built: AlertDialogMedia and the size="sm" two-column footer. Both are real exports with no consumer in the corpus... [AlertDialogSize] records the second so a caller can ask for it." The enum value exists but AlertDialogFooter never reads it, so requesting the sm two-column footer on Flutter silently gets the normal end-aligned row instead — a genuine, acknowledged anatomy gap, not merely undocumented.

api.flutter: enum AlertDialogSize { normal, sm } is accepted by AlertDialogContent.size but, per the anatomy gap above, `sm` only affects ConstrainedBox(maxWidth: Containers.xs) and does not reach AlertDialogFooter, which has no size parameter at all.
api.web: AlertDialogContent({size = "default"}: {size?: "default" | "sm"}) sets data-size on the content AND AlertDialogFooter reads group-data-[size=sm]/alert-dialog-content:grid-cols-2 off that same data attribute, so size drives both the width and the footer layout.

states.flutter: AlertDialogAction.loading swaps in presumably a spinner via Button(loading:true) and sets onPressed: loading ? null : onPressed, per the file's own reasoning about Button asChild's silent no-op on the web being why loading is declared locally.
states.web: AlertDialogAction sets data-loading, aria-busy={loading || undefined}, disabled={disabled || loading}, and renders <Spinner aria-hidden/> before ButtonLabel when loading.
states.note: Both sides independently declare `loading` on the Action component (rather than inheriting Button's, for the identical asChild/Slot reasoning stated in both files' comments) and use it to block a second press.

disabled.flutter: AlertDialogContent/Header/Footer carry no disabled field; only AlertDialogAction's loading indirectly disables via onPressed: null.
disabled.web: The alert-dialog doc page's States grid marks a "disabled trigger" only at the Button level (audited separately) and marks success/error/empty N/A on the dialog itself.
disabled.note: The dialog shell itself has no disabled state on either platform; disabling belongs to the trigger Button (a separately audited component) or to AlertDialogAction's loading path, already covered under states.

interaction.flutter: AlertDialogAction/Cancel unconditionally wrap the button in `Tooltip(label: tooltip ?? label, child: Button(...))` with no truncation check anywhere in alert_dialog.dart or tooltip.dart (grep for truncat/scrollWidth in tooltip.dart returns nothing) — every non-null label always shows a tooltip on hover/focus.
interaction.web: useLabelIsTruncated() measures `label.scrollWidth > label.clientWidth + 1` via a ResizeObserver on the button's own [data-slot="button-label"], and `mayOpen = tooltip != null || truncated` gates the automatic label-as-tooltip so it opens only when the label is genuinely clipped (the explicit `tooltip` prop still always shows).

ORIGINAL: The alert-dialog doc page itself documents this as a fixed bug: "That tooltip attaches only when the label is actually clipped... Radix focuses Cancel automatically when an alert dialog opens, so attaching the tooltip unconditionally meant a tooltip repeating the button's own words appeared before the user did anything, and swallowed the first Escape." Flutter's alert_dialog.dart top-of-file doc even records this as a known, deliberately-reproduced drift ("on this page nothing truncates, and it fires anyway") rather than the truncation-gated behaviour the current web source actually implements — so Flutter over-triggers the automatic tooltip (and correspondingly swallows an extra Escape) on every non-truncated label, which the web no longer does.

semantics.flutter: _Dialog wraps its content in Semantics(label: '$title. $description', container: true); AlertDialog.build uses OverlayPortal(..., dismissOnOverlayTap: false, ...) — measured refusing overlay-tap dismissal per the library doc.
semantics.web: role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true" set by Radix's AlertDialogPrimitive.Content; aria-labelledby/aria-describedby wired to AlertDialogTitle/Description; onPointerDownOutside and onInteractOutside both call preventDefault() so overlay clicks do nothing.
semantics.note: Combined accessible name/description and the disabled-overlay-dismissal behaviour both match; Flutter folds title+description into one Semantics label rather than separate labelledby/describedby nodes, which is a reasonable platform difference given Flutter's Semantics tree has no direct aria-describedby equivalent, and does not change what is ultimately announced.
